short: A hole in your opponent's camp, protected by one of your pawns.
body: A knight on an outpost is frequently the best piece on the board. It cannot be attacked by a pawn, it is defended by one of yours, and it sits inside the enemy position where it cramps everything.

The manoeuvre to get one is usually three moves long and contains no tactics at all: identify the [[hole]], remove whatever piece defends it, then walk a knight there. Trading a bishop for the knight that guards the square is normally a good deal, even though it looks like a concession.
Bishops can occupy outposts too, but knights benefit most — a bishop covers the same diagonal from a distance, whereas a knight has to be close to do anything.

diagram.caption: d5 is the outpost; the knight on f6 is the only thing still guarding it.
